title: Final twisted-arrow resolution of a cartesian fibration with terminal fibres
statement:
Use quasicategories, ordinary nerves, coherent functors, transformations and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $A$ be a small ordinary category and let $p:R\to N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$ be a cartesian fibration of quasicategories in a containing universe. Suppose that each fibre $R_a$ has a terminal object $t_a$, meaning that $\operatorname{Map}_{R_a}(r,t_a)$ is contractible for every $r\in R_a$. No transport-preservation assumption on these terminal objects is made. For $u:a\to b$ in $A$, write $u^*:R_a\to R_b$ for cartesian transport along $u^{\mathrm{op}}:b\to a$ in $N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$.

Define $K_A=N(\operatorname{Tw}(A)^{\mathrm{op}})$ as follows: its objects are arrows $u:a\to b$ of $A$, and an arrow $u\to u'$ is a pair $f:a\to a'$, $g:b'\to b$ with $u=gu'f$. There is a coherent functor $k:K_A\to R$ over the projection $u:a\to b\mapsto b$ to $N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$, with $k(u)\simeq u^*t_a$. On the arrow $(f,g)$ its component is the composite
$$u^*t_a\simeq g^*u'^*f^*t_a\longrightarrow g^*u'^*t_{a'}\longrightarrow u'^*t_{a'},$$
where the middle map is induced by the map to the terminal object $t_{a'}$ and the last arrow is cartesian over $g^{\mathrm{op}}$. The compatible terminal-object and cartesian-lift choices can be made coherently, and any two such constructions are naturally equivalent over $N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$.

This functor $k$ is final in the following strong sense. For every quasicategory $D$ in any further containing universe, coherent diagram $V:R\to D$ and $d\in D$, restriction itself induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(R,D)}(V,\Delta_Rd)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K_A,D)}(Vk,\Delta_{K_A}d),$$
natural in $V,d$. Consequently a specified cocone on $V$ is colimiting if and only if its restriction along $k$ is colimiting; existence of either colimit implies existence of the other with that cocone. The total $R$ and its mapping spaces need not be small in the universe in which $A$ is small.

source.place: Agent terminal-fibre generalization of the twisted-diagonal contraction in Section 5.6, Proposition 5.6.9, pp. 241-242. The statement here is for a given cartesian fibration, not a classification theorem; see report.md for the comma contraction and the distinction from the source assertion. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical lemma.

proof.text:
First make the construction, retaining its coherences. Opposite the arrow-projection theorem [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-arrow-projection]: the category of cartesian edges projects by target and base edge as a trivial Kan fibration onto all such pairs, since $p$ is cartesian. Its boundary-lifting property lets us choose compatible cartesian lifts over every simplex, also relative to choices already made on faces and with simplicial parameters. The opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] identifies composites of these lifts with lifts of composite base arrows. For every chain $a_0\xrightarrow{f_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{f_n}a_n$ in $A$, choose in the last fibre the comparison to $t_{a_n}$ from the transported earlier terminal objects. For $n=1$ it is $f_1^*t_{a_0}\to t_{a_1}$. At every higher stage the already chosen faces, after factoring through the chosen cartesian edges, are a boundary with last vertex $t_{a_n}$; [lem-cbc-terminal-boundary-extension] fills it. Applying the transport functors to these terminal comparison simplices gives the required comparison simplices in the other fibres. For a chain of twisted squares $(f_i,g_i)$, combine these simplices with the chosen cartesian lifts over the chain of $g_i^{\mathrm{op}}$. The cartesian universal property [lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-mapping-fiber] factors each comparison through its lift, including its triangle data, and the preceding relative boundary construction makes the faces and degeneracies agree. This constructs $k$ with $k(u)=u^*t_a$ up to the chosen equivalence. Its edge on $(f,g)$ is exactly
$$u^*t_a\simeq g^*u'^*f^*t_a\longrightarrow g^*u'^*t_{a'}\longrightarrow u'^*t_{a'}.$$
Apply the same relative construction with a parameter interval to two choices, and with parameter boundaries to their comparisons. Terminal objects form a contractible Kan complex by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], and cartesian-lift choices have the boundary-lifting property just used. Thus the two constructions admit a coherent natural comparison over the base, whose components are equivalences; the componentwise criterion in that node makes it a natural equivalence. No assertion that $f^*t_a$ is terminal is used.

source.place: Agent construction from terminal comparisons and cartesian lifts; the twisted-diagonal comparison of Proposition 5.6.9 is motivation, not an assertion of this generalization.

proof.text:
Fix $r\in R_c$. Use the join comma $C_r=K_A\times_R R_{r/}$, where an $n$-simplex of $R_{r/}$ is a map $\Delta^0\star\Delta^n\to R$ restricting to $r$ on the first vertex, and the projection restricts to the last face. Thus an $n$-simplex of $C_r$ is a simplex $v:\Delta^n\to K_A$ together with precisely such a cone whose last face is $kv$; its face and degeneracy maps are restrictions. This definition retains all comma triangles and their higher compatibilities. By the opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], the projection $R_{r/}\to R$ is a left fibration. Its pullback to the quasicategory $K_A$ fills inner horns by first filling in $K_A$ and then lifting, so $C_r$ is a quasicategory. An object is $(u:a\to b,\beta:r\to k(u))$. Its base edge is uniquely $w^{\mathrm{op}}:c\to b$ for an arrow $w:b\to c$ of $A$, because mapping spaces of an ordinary nerve are discrete Hom sets. The cartesian edge $(wu)^*t_a\to u^*t_a$ over $w^{\mathrm{op}}$ gives, by [lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-mapping-fiber], a coherent factorization of $\beta$ as
$$r\xrightarrow{h}(wu)^*t_a\longrightarrow u^*t_a,$$
with $h$ in $R_c$. In particular the space of factorizations of the fixed $\beta$, including its comparison homotopy, is contractible. For an edge, the comparison triangle is a last-horn problem $\Lambda^2_2\to R$: its two given edges are $\beta$ and the cartesian edge $(wu)^*t_a\to u^*t_a$. Its base triangle is fixed, and the cartesian-edge clause of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] supplies $h$ and the triangle. Over a simplex of the join comma, factor the corresponding cone along the compatible cartesian lifts from step 1. Induct on its dimension, keeping the already chosen faces: the remaining lifting problems have the same last cartesian edge and are the higher last-horn problems in that definition. These fillers retain the entire cone at $r$, not just the induced homotopy classes. Degenerate simplices are assigned the degeneracies of the chosen fillers; choose fillers only on nondegenerate simplices. This constructs compatible factorizations on whole parameter simplices. Define $H:C_r\to C_r$ by
$$H(u,w,\beta)=(wu:a\to c,h:r\to (wu)^*t_a).$$
On a comma arrow with twisted pair $(f:a\to a',g:b'\to b)$, the base triangle says $w'=wg$. Hence $wu=w'u'f$, and $H$ uses the twisted pair $(f,1_c)$ together with the lifted triangle. Cartesian factorization makes these lifted triangles compatible under composition and all higher simplices. All this is done over a fixed $r$, so no local smallness in the universe of $A$ is required.

source.place: Agent comma calculation for the terminal-fibre generalization of Section 5.6; factorization of the base edge and its parameter simplices.

proof.text:
There is a coherent transformation $H\to\mathrm{id}_{C_r}$. At $(u,w,\beta)$ it is the twisted arrow $(1_a,w):wu\to u$, with its cartesian factorization triangle $\beta\simeq (\mathrm{cart}_w)h$. Choose a terminal cone in $R_c$ by [lem-coef-infinity-normalized-final-cone]. Write $\rho:r\to t_c$ for its component at $r$, and put $z=(1_c:c\to c,\rho)$ in $C_r$. There is a second coherent transformation $H\to\Delta z$: its twisted pair is $(wu,1_c):wu\to1_c$, and its triangle compares $r\xrightarrow h(wu)^*t_a\to t_c$ with $\rho$. The comparison to $t_c$ here is the one used to construct $k$ in step 1. The terminal-boundary extension theorem gives these triangles and all their parameter coherences relative to that chosen comparison; no equality of two arbitrarily chosen maps to $t_c$ is asserted. On an arrow of $C_r$ the required equality of twisted pairs is $(w'u')f=wu$, already established in step 2. Thus the two transformations give a zigzag
$$\mathrm{id}_{C_r}\ \longleftarrow\ H\ \longrightarrow\ \Delta z.$$
On realizations they are homotopies: triangulate each prism $|\Delta^n|\times[0,1]$ by its monotone lattice paths and evaluate the transformation on the corresponding simplices of $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$. The face restrictions agree, so these maps descend through the realization quotient. Concatenating the first one backwards with the second contracts the identity to the constant map at $z$. Consequently $C_r$ is weakly contractible. This is a contraction of the whole coherent comma category, including all higher simplices, rather than only of its homotopy category.

source.place: Agent explicit twisted-comma contraction: replace the arrow u by wu and then map wu to the identity of c.

proof.text:
To obtain restriction on cocone spaces without a circular appeal to an existing cofinality theorem, enlarge to a universe in which $R$ is small and factor $k$ by the small-object theorem [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization], using the set of right horns $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0<i\leq n$. In simplicial sets colimits are computed degreewise. Each horn is generated by finitely many nondegenerate simplices, so its maps into an increasing countable sequence of horn-cell inclusions factor at a finite stage; equality of two such maps is also detected at a finite stage. Thus the smallness hypothesis holds with $\kappa=\aleph_0$. The theorem gives
$$K_A\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}R,\qquad qj=k,$$
where $j$ is a right-horn cell map and $q$ lifts all right horns. In the terminology of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne] and [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], $j$ is right anodyne and $q$ is a right fibration. Since $R$ is a quasicategory, filling an inner horn first in $R$ and then along $q$ proves that $E$ is a quasicategory. All sets of attaching squares are small in the chosen enlarged universe.

source.place: Agent use of the one-sided horn small-object factorization; compare the factorization characterization before Proposition 4.4.4.

proof.text:
Let $S_r=R_{r/}$ be the join coslice. By the opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], its target projection $S_r\to R$ is a left fibration. By the explicit simplex definition in step 2, $K_A\times_R S_r=C_r$ as simplicial sets; no comparison between distinct comma models is required. Put $D_r=E\times_R S_r$. The pullback of $j$ along the left fibration $D_r\to E$ is
$$K_A\times_R S_r\longrightarrow D_r.$$
It is right anodyne by [lem-coef-left-fibration-right-anodyne-base-change]. The Kan-Quillen theorem [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] makes every horn inclusion a trivial cofibration and closes these under cell attachments and retracts. Hence this pullback is a weak homotopy equivalence. Step 3 implies that $D_r$ is weakly contractible.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.11 with Proposition 4.4.4(iv), plus the agent right-anodyne comparison of comma models.

proof.text: The identity arrow is initial in $S_r$ by the opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-equivalence-final]. Its normalized initial cone, supplied by the opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-normalized-final-cone], is a transformation from the constant identity arrow to the identity functor of $S_r$, constant on its initial vertex. The projection $D_r\to S_r$ is the pullback of the right fibration $q$. Its edges are cartesian: the defining right-horn lifting property includes every cartesian-edge horn problem. To regard the initial join cone as a transformation, precompose on each simplex with the prism map $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^0\star\Delta^n$ that sends $(a,0)$ to the initial vertex and $(a,1)$ to the vertex $a$ of the last block. These maps agree with faces and degeneracies, and the transformation is constant on the initial vertex $1_r$. Pull it back along $D_r\to S_r$, with target the projection $D_r\to S_r$. Together with the target diagram $\mathrm{id}_{D_r}$ it defines a map from $D_r$ into the base of the cartesian-arrow projection for $D_r\to S_r$. Every required target admits a cartesian lift: the right $1$-horn lifts any edge with prescribed target, and every edge of a right fibration is cartesian by the last-horn definition. The opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-arrow-projection] therefore makes this arrow projection a trivial Kan fibration onto the whole required base. On the simplicial subset $E_r\subseteq D_r$, prescribe the lift to be the degenerate arrow at each simplex of $E_r$; this is possible because the normalized cone there is constant. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to this inclusion and the arrow projection. The resulting relative lift has source in the fibre over $1_r$, exactly $E_r$. It gives $T:D_r\to E_r$ and a transformation $iT\to\mathrm{id}_{D_r}$ whose restriction to $E_r$ is degenerate, so $Ti=\mathrm{id}_{E_r}$ strictly. The transformation supplies a simplicial interval homotopy on $D_r$; the equality supplies the constant interval homotopy on $E_r$. By [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak], $i$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Thus $E_r$ is weakly contractible by step 5, and it is Kan by [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers]. This holds for every $r\in R$, so [lem-coef-right-fibration-contractible-fibers] makes $q$ a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Agent deformation of the right-fibration comma onto its fibre, using the initial identity arrow; no classification or space-valued straightening theorem.

proof.text:
A trivial Kan fibration $q:E\to R$ has a section $s$ by [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms], applied to the empty inclusion into $R$. Let $J$ be the ordinary groupoid on two objects with one arrow between each ordered pair. Use the same lifting theorem on $E\times\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow E\times N(J)$, with endpoints $\mathrm{id}_E$ and $sq$ and base map $q\operatorname{pr}_E$. The lift supplies a coherent natural equivalence between these endpoints: the interval arrows in $N(J)$ are invertible, so their images are equivalences. Thus $q$ and $s$ are inverse functor equivalences, and whiskering gives inverse equivalences on the corresponding functor quasicategories. The mapping-space clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore makes restriction along $q$ an equivalence on cocone spaces for any $V:R\to D$ and $d\in D$. Restriction along $j$ is an equivalence on those spaces by [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones]. Their composite is restriction itself along $qj=k$, proving the displayed equivalence in the statement, naturally in $V,d$ and coherently with postcomposition in $d$.

For a specified cocone $\lambda:V\to\Delta d$, the mapping-space criterion for colimits in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] tests whether $\operatorname{Map}_D(d,x)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(R,D)}(V,\Delta x)$ is an equivalence for every $x$. The restriction equivalences just proved identify this test with that for $\lambda k$. This proves both directions. If a colimit cocone is initially given only on $Vk$, the equivalence of cocone spaces with its fixed apex lifts it to a cocone on $V$ up to coherent equivalence, which is colimiting by the same criterion. The reverse implication is restriction. The factorization was performed in an enlarged universe containing the entire $R$, independently of the smaller universe of $A$. For any specified further target universe, take one containing it and this factorization; every construction is a simplicial map and the comparisons are the actual restriction maps, so the conclusion applies to each $D$ asserted in the statement.

source.place: Agent conclusion from right-anodyne factorization; compare the cocone restriction formulation of Theorem 6.4.5. The proof does not cite the downstream comma-cofinality criterion.
